root_cause.text: In tpacket_snd(), the vnet_hdr pointer is set to point directly into the mmap’d TX ring buffer that is writable by userspace, and the kernel validates it via __packet_snd_vnet_parse() but later re-reads the same fields from userspace memory in virtio_net_hdr_to_skb(), allowing a concurrent thread to modify the header between the two accesses and bypass validation.
root_cause.evidence: The commit description states: "vnet_hdr points directly into the mmap'd TX ring buffer shared with userspace. The kernel validates the header via __packet_snd_vnet_parse() but then re-reads all fields later in virtio_net_hdr_to_skb(). A concurrent userspace thread can modify the vnet_hdr fields between validation and use, bypassing all safety checks." The patch resolves this by copying vnet_hdr to a stack-local variable before validation and using that copy afterwards.

bic_trace_step.reason: The commit adds tpacket_snd support for PACKET_VNET_HDR with PACKET_TX_RING. In tpacket_snd(), vnet_hdr is set to point directly into userspace-mapped frame data (line 'vnet_hdr = data;'). The kernel validates it via __packet_snd_vnet_parse() (line 8), but later reuses the same pointer in packet_snd_vnet_gso(skb, vnet_hdr) (line 40) without copying the header into kernel memory. This creates a time-of-check-to-time-of-use (TOCTOU) vulnerability where a concurrent thread can modify the vnet_hdr fields after validation and before the second read, bypassing validation. No fix (e.g., copying the header) is present in this commit.
